about: r31fix-pairs-none-001-s0n1 answered true on six stands and false on three, in either class of the GENERAL route. Here each child of the nested set s0n1 reads a GENERAL marker of its own before anything else in one of its rules: s0n1p0 reads subject.parityR32SeenP0, the nested set s0n1n1 subject.parityR32SeenN1, the nested set s0n1n2 subject.parityR32SeenN2. A marker answers m. It is read where it cannot change a rule's outcome: in the ALLOW rule r19 of s0n1n2 as its whole condition, <marker> CONTAINS 'm' (r19's condition was true), and elsewhere as a false first conjunct before the absent resource key the rule read first. Each case but r32open-s0n1-only-n2 asks the check of i1 three times, classed by one marker's route: a stand's goldens say which children it evaluated and what it answered. If s0n1, which has no combiningAlgorithm, answers by its first applicable child in the stand's order, only that child's marker is read and the check is true only when it is s0n1n2; if the nested INACTIVE set s0n1n2 takes no part on a stand, its marker is not read and the check is false. Read as DENY_UNLESS_PERMIT, with the status of a nested set ignored, every check is true and s0n1n2's marker is read on every stand.
